description_ru: Биография Юрия Гагарина: от деревенского мальчика до первого человека, полетевшего в космос в 1961 году.
text:
Yuri Gagarin was the first human being in space. On 12 April 1961, he flew around the Earth in a small round spacecraft, and the whole world listened to his name. Many people know this story, but fewer people know how he lived before that famous day.

Yuri was born on 9 March 1934, in a small village called Klushino, west of Moscow. His father was a carpenter, and his mother worked on a farm. The family lived in a simple wooden house. When Yuri was seven, the Second World War came to his village. German soldiers took the house and the family had to live in a small hut for almost two years. His older brother and sister were taken away to work in Germany, and Yuri never forgot those hard years.

After the war, he went back to school and became a good student. He loved mathematics and physics, and his teachers remembered him as a cheerful and friendly boy. When he was fifteen, he left his village and went to a technical school near Moscow, where he learned to make things from metal. A few years later he studied in the city of Saratov, and there he joined a flying club. In his first flight, he sat in a small plane next to an instructor, and he felt that his life was going to change.

In 1955 he joined the air force and trained as a military pilot. He was not a tall man. He was only about 1.57 metres tall, and this was a great advantage, because the space capsules were very small. In 1957, he married Valentina, a young medical worker, and later they had two daughters, Yelena and Galina. Then, in the same year, the Soviet Union sent the first satellite, Sputnik, into space. Yuri watched the news with excitement. He wanted to be part of the future.

In 1960, the country was looking for the first men to fly into space. More than three thousand pilots were considered. Doctors tested every one of them, and the tests were much harder than any normal examination. Candidates sat in spinning machines, stayed in silent rooms and went into very hot or very cold chambers. In the end, only twenty men were chosen. Yuri was one of them, and later he became the first choice for the flight. His quick mind and his warm smile helped him. The other men said he was easier to like than anyone else.

The big day arrived on 12 April 1961. Early in the morning, Yuri put on his orange spacesuit and rode to the launch place at Baikonur. Before the rocket left, he said one short word to the engineers: "Poyekhali!" It means "Let's go!" The rocket lifted off, and Yuri's ship, Vostok 1, went up higher and faster than any human had ever travelled. In only eight minutes, he was in space.

Yuri circled the Earth once. The whole flight lasted one hour and forty-eight minutes. He looked through the small window and saw the blue planet below him. "The Earth is blue," he told the controllers. "How wonderful. It is amazing." He ate a little food from a tube and wrote notes with a pencil. Then the ship came back down. At about seven kilometres above the ground, Yuri left the capsule and used a parachute. He landed in a field near the Volga River, and the first people who saw him were a woman and her granddaughter. They were afraid of the strange man in the orange suit, but he said, "Don't be afraid! I'm a Soviet man like you."

Yuri became a hero immediately. He travelled to many countries, and crowds waited in the streets to see him. In London, he met the Queen. He was always polite and humble, and he never forgot ordinary people. But he found fame tiring. He missed flying, and he returned to training. He wanted to fly in space again, and he also studied at the Air Force Academy.

Sadly, he never went back to space. On 27 March 1968, Yuri died in a training flight in a jet near Moscow. He was only thirty-four years old. The whole country mourned for him.

Today, people remember Yuri Gagarin every year on 12 April, which is celebrated as the International Day of Human Space Flight. His flight proved that people could live and work beyond our planet, and it opened the way for later astronauts. He was brave, and he was kind. Most important, he showed that a boy from a small village could reach the stars.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Кончик языка поднят и не касается нёба, губы чуть округлены. Не раскатывайте русское «р».
Кончик языка слегка между зубами, воздух проходит без голоса. Не заменяйте звук на «с» или «ф».
Короткий звук, похожий на «а» без напряжения, рот полуоткрыт.

questions.question: Where was Yuri Gagarin born?
questions.answer: He was born in a small village called Klushino, near Moscow.

questions.question: Why was his height an advantage?
questions.answer: The space capsules were very small, and he was only about 1.57 metres tall.

questions.question: What did he say before the rocket left?
How long did the first flight last?
questions.answer: It lasted one hour and forty-eight minutes.
